data.hypothesis: A 32x4 CTA with an 8-row output tile keeps two outputs per thread but halves the CTA size relative to the selected 16x8 parent, at the cost of twice as many Y blocks and more halo loads per output. The catalog has four distinct valid programs: 16x4 measured 2.816 µs, the selected 16x8 parent 3.223 µs, 8x8 measured 3.359 µs, and 32x8 measured 3.335 µs. Those small, variable samples do not establish a cause; this new 8x4 configuration tests whether smaller CTAs and reduced tile work per block offset the extra loading and scheduling.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use as context when choosing a new tile/launch contrast; the measurements do not establish causality.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured 16x4 variant was faster on average than the 16x8 parent and the 8x8 and 32x8 variants, but the samples are limited and variable. A new launch configuration should test a distinct scheduling assumption rather than repeat those shapes.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this 8x4 configuration with the official protocol after oracle validation, then compare repeated timings against the baseline and selected parent.

data.notes: Proposes one source-only launch/tile experiment; no local build, oracle validation, or timing was performed. The controller should validate signed varying inputs with independent endpoint values and collect the official repeated full-run timings.
transformations: Change the Y output tile from 16 rows to 8 while retaining 32 contiguous X lanes.
Use 4 Y threads per CTA, so each thread loads four of the 16 shared rows and computes two output rows; every tile row, including halos, is initialized before synchronization.
Launch a 32x4 CTA over two X tiles, eight Y tiles, and all 64 z planes; retain the exact stencil expression and q<0 / q>63 period-63 mapping.
